Prepare vendor payment schedules and banking instructions for authorised approval. Maintain banking documents and coordinate routine queries with banks. Monitor cash and bank balances and report upcoming payment requirements. 5. Invoicing & Commercial Documents Prepare quotations, proforma invoices, sales invoices, credit notes and debit notes as required. Verify invoices against purchase orders, agreed prices, payment terms and delivery records. Prepare or coordinate e-invoices, e-way bills, delivery challans and supporting documents where applicable. Coordinate with sales, purchase and dispatch teams for accurate and timely billing. 6. Receivables, Payables & Documentation Follow up on customer payments and reconcile customer and vendor accounts. Maintain ageing reports and highlight overdue balances. Organise invoices, vouchers, purchase orders, bank records and statutory documents. Provide records and schedules for audits, assessments and CA reviews. Maintain confidentiality and follow company approval procedures. 
 Preferred candidate profile Strong practical knowledge of Tally Prime and MS Excel. Hands-on experience in GST, TDS, bank reconciliation and monthly accounts closing. Ability to prepare and explain P&L statements and accounting reports. Good attention to detail, communication and follow-up skills. Ability to manage deadlines and work independently. Experience in manufacturing, trading or export businesses is an advantage. Performance Expectations Accurate, up-to-date books with complete supporting documents. title: IT Operations - Manager
description:
Were proud to be recognized as a Great Place to Work , a testament to our inclusive culture, strong leadership, and commitment to employee well-being and growth. At Tarento, you ll be part of a collaborative environment where ideas are valued, learning is continuous, and careers are built on passion and purpose. 
 
 Job Description - IT Operations / IT Manager 
 Location: Bangalore| Experience: 10+ years |Team: 5-8 IT professionals | User base: ~500-person IT organization 
 About the Role We are seeking a highly experienced and proactive IT Operations Lead / IT Manager to lead and optimize the technology environment supporting a 500-person IT organization. The role combines strategic IT leadership with hands-on operational ownership across infrastructure, IT service management, end-user computing, cloud, DevOps, cybersecurity, compliance, vendor management, automation, and technology governance. The successful candidate will lead a team of 5-8 IT professionals, ensure stable and secure day-to-day operations, and drive continuous improvement, automation, cost optimization, and exceptional service delivery. 
 1. IT Operations, Service Management & Service Delivery Lead day-to-day IT operations, ensuring availability, performance, reliability, resilience, and security of infrastructure, systems, applications, networks, cloud services, and end-user technology. Own IT Service Management processes covering Incident, Problem, Change, Request, and Service Management through the IT ticketing platform. Establish, govern, and continuously improve SLAs, KPIs, ticket ageing, response/resolution targets, and user satisfaction. Act as the escalation point for critical and major incidents; coordinate troubleshooting, root-cause analysis, corrective actions, and post-incident reviews. Drive continuous service improvement aligned with ITIL best practices and business priorities. Develop monthly SLA and operational reports covering Internet uptime, service uptime, ticket volumes, ageing, resolution performance, and recurring issues. Maintain a strong customer-service culture and provide empathetic, professional support to internal users. 2. Team Leadership & People Management Lead, mentor, coach, and develop a team of 5-8 IT support and infrastructure professionals. Assign work, establish priorities, monitor performance, manage escalations, and ensure timely resolution of IT issues. Define objectives, KPIs, development plans, knowledge-sharing practices, and operational ownership across the team. Foster a collaborative, supportive, accountable, and continuous-improvement-oriented culture. Coordinate cross-functional teams during major incidents, audits, projects, technology changes, and transformation initiatives. 3. IT Infrastructure, Network & End-User Computing Oversee enterprise infrastructure including networks, servers, storage, virtualization, wireless, firewalls, cloud environments, and end-user devices. Ensure high availability and reliability of critical IT systems and services. Manage wireless access points, hardware firewalls, switches, network equipment, Internet circuits, and associated vendor services. Manage the complete lifecycle of laptops, desktops, mobiles, peripherals, and accessories from procurement and provisioning through refresh and secure disposal. Own user onboarding, role changes, access provisioning, offboarding, asset recovery, and access-card coordination with HR. Perform monthly Internet bandwidth and capacity checks and recommend upgrades based on usage and business demand. Maintain disk-capacity and infrastructure-health reports and proactively address capacity risks. 4. Cloud Management & Cost Optimization Manage and optimize cloud resources across AWS, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud Platform (GCP), where applicable. Support cloud services and customer-facing workloads hosted on AWS, Azure, and GCP. Monitor availability, performance, capacity, security, and operational health of cloud resources. Track monthly cloud bills, analyze consumption trends, forecast spend, and drive FinOps-style cost optimization. Define cloud adoption standards and ensure appropriate governance, tagging, access controls, backup, and lifecycle management. Balance on-premises and cloud workloads to optimize performance, scalability, resilience, and total cost of ownership. 5. Software, License, Patch & Configuration Management Manage Microsoft 365/O365 licenses and project-specific software licenses, including allocation, renewal, usage, and cost optimization. Oversee software deployment, application inventory, endpoint configuration, and patch management using tools such as ManageEngine Desktop Central/Endpoint Central. Implement and govern automated OS patching for employee workstations and servers. Maintain accurate software and hardware inventories and ensure appropriate licensing compliance. Track software renewals, support contracts, certificates, and technology lifecycle milestones. 6. DevOps, Git & CI/CD Operations Provide operational leadership and governance for DevOps tooling and practices. Manage and support Git, GitLab, Jenkins, GitHub Actions, and Azure DevOps environments as applicable. Perform periodic Git/GitLab access reviews and ensure least-privilege access and appropriate segregation of duties. Support CI/CD pipelines, automation, deployment reliability, and operational stability in collaboration with development and DevOps teams. Lead infrastructure-as-code and configuration-management practices using Terraform and Ansible where applicable. Support containerization and orchestration platforms such as Docker and Kubernetes. 7. Cybersecurity, Risk & Compliance Define and implement IT security policies, standards, procedures, and operational controls. Act as the IT/security escalation point and support enterprise security governance and risk management. Conduct vulnerability checks and coordinate remediation of identified vulnerabilities. Manage endpoint protection and antivirus/EDR platforms such as Cortex and ensure security agents remain healthy and current. Oversee identity and access management, privileged access, access reviews, endpoint security, network security, and incident response. Maintain the Information Security Management System (ISMS) and support ISO 27001 certification and audit requirements. Participate in quarterly audits, evidence collection, remediation tracking, and management reviews. Coordinate cybersecurity incidents, containment, investigation, recovery, and lessons learned. 8. Enterprise Architecture, Technology Strategy & Governance Define and govern enterprise IT architecture standards, technology reference models, and infrastructure principles. Establish vendor evaluation frameworks and technology selection criteria. Define cloud adoption policies, technology lifecycle standards, and application rationalization roadmaps aligned with business strategy. Partner with C-suite and executive leadership to translate business objectives into technology roadmaps and investment priorities. Present IT performance metrics, risk posture, cybersecurity status, governance outcomes, and strategic initiatives to senior leadership. Evaluate emerging technologies, including AI, automation, AIOps, and cloud platforms, and assess their operational and business value. 9. AI, AIOps & Automation Lead adoption of AIOps capabilities such as ML-based event correlation, anomaly detection, predictive monitoring, and automated first-line remediation. Drive AI-powered ITSM capabilities including intelligent ticket classification, AI-driven routing, NLP-based resolution recommendations, and predictive SLA-breach alerts. Identify opportunities to automate repetitive IT operations, support processes, monitoring, reporting, and remediation activities. Architect and manage infrastructure for AI workloads, including on-premises GPU platforms and cost-optimized cloud AI services where appropriate. Measure operational improvements from AI and automation initiatives, including reduced downtime, faster MTTR, and lower operating cost. 10. Proactive Maintenance, Upgrades & Business Continuity Plan and execute quarterly firmware upgrades for wireless access points and network equipment. Implement and maintain automated OS patching and upgrade cycles for end-user systems and servers. Perform planned server OS upgrades and maintain application/platform upgrade schedules. Perform quarterly GitLab version upgrades with appropriate validation, backup, rollback, and change-management controls. Maintain backup, disaster recovery, business continuity, and infrastructure resilience plans for critical services. Use monitoring and capacity data to identify and resolve issues before they impact users or customers. 11. Monitoring, Reporting & Operational Governance Develop and maintain monthly IT dashboards covering service uptime, Internet uptime, network bandwidth, patch compliance, license renewals, ticket performance, disk usage, cloud spend, and security posture. Produce monthly SLA and KPI reports for leadership and relevant stakeholders. Maintain operational dashboards and trend analysis to identify recurring incidents, capacity risks, cost anomalies, and improvement opportunities. Maintain accurate IT documentation, asset records, service ownership information, escalation matrices, and operational runbooks. Maintain and share access-card server details with HR in accordance with access governance procedures. 12. Procurement, Vendor & Contract Management Own procurement of IT hardware, software, licenses, accessories, network equipment, and technology services. Manage vendor, MSP, telecom, cloud, and technology-partner relationships. Define and monitor vendor SLAs, KPIs, contracts, renewals, service quality, and operational performance. Lead vendor evaluations, commercial negotiations, renewals, and corrective actions in collaboration with procurement and leadership. Ensure third-party services meet requirements for availability, security, compliance, performance, and cost. 13. IT Budget & Financial Management Own IT CapEx and OpEx planning, forecasting, budget tracking, and financial reporting. Manage cloud spend forecasting and optimization across AWS, Azure, and GCP. Optimize software licensing, infrastructure, telecom, support, and vendor costs without compromising service quality or security. Present technology investment proposals and cost-benefit analysis to leadership. 14. Client & Stakeholder Interaction Participate in client calls and technical discussions as required. Provide service status, operational updates, logs, evidence, and technical information to clients in coordination with relevant teams. Translate technical issues into clear business impact, resolution status, risk, and next steps for non-technical stakeholders. Build strong relationships with business leaders, customers, vendors, and internal technology teams. Preferred Qualifications & Certifications ITIL 4 certification. ISO 27001 Lead Implementer or Lead Auditor; CISSP or CISM is advantageous. AWS, Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud certifications. CompTIA or other infrastructure/security certifications. TOGAF or equivalent enterprise architecture certification. PMP/PRINCE2 or equivalent project-management certification. Terraform, Kubernetes, or DevOps-related certifications. Key Competencies IT Operations Leadership Infrastructure & Network Management Cloud & FinOps IT Service Management & ITIL Cybersecurity & Compliance DevOps & Automation AI/AIOps & Intelligent IT Operations Enterprise Architecture & Technology Strategy Vendor & Contract Management Budget & Cost Management Problem-Solving & Incident Management Customer Service & Empathy Executive Communication & Stakeholder Management Proactive Approach & Continuous Improvement Team Leadership & People Development Key Performance Indicators IT infrastructure and service availability / uptime. SLA compliance, ticket resolution time, backlog, and user satisfaction. Major incident frequency, MTTR, recurrence, and root-cause closure. Patch compliance and vulnerability remediation performance. Cloud spend against budget and measurable cost optimization. Software/license compliance and renewal management. Vendor/MSP performance against contractual SLAs. Audit findings, security compliance, and ISO 27001/ISMS performance. Change success rate and change-related incidents. Automation/AIOps adoption and measurable reduction in downtime and operational effort. Successful delivery of infrastructure upgrades, lifecycle activities, and technology roadmaps. Role Impact The IT Manager / IT Operations Lead is accountable for building a stable, secure, scalable, cost-effective, and business-aligned IT environment. The role combines strong operational discipline with strategic technology leadership, proactive service improvement, automation, cybersecurity governance, cloud optimization, and people leadership. The successful candidate will help transform IT into a highly reliable, measurable, customer-focused, and continuously improving technology function. 
 Required Skills IT Infrastructure cybersecurity, compliance IT service management vendor management end-user computing compliance devops

title: Treasury Manager
description:
Job Summary Everpure (NYSE: P) has evolved from storage pioneer to data platform, closing fiscal 2026 with billion in revenue, its first billion-dollar quarter, and accelerating growth into FY27. Our strategic agenda spans the companies defining the next era of technology - hyperscalers, AI labs, the AI hardware supply chain, data platform providers, and the broader AI ecosystem. This type of work-work that changes the world-is what the tech industry was founded on. So, if you're ready to seize the endless opportunities and leave your mark, come join us. The Role As our International Treasury Manager, you will shape and safeguard Everpures financial foundation across international entities. Partnering closely with Accounting, Tax, FP&A, Legal, Payroll and Accounts Payable, you will lead regional cash management, optimize intercompany liquidity, and scale high-impact banking infrastructure. You will leverage AI-enabled tools and automated workflows to transform cross-border financial operations into a seamless, high-performing growth engine. This role offers the unique opportunity to drive capital efficiency, mitigate risk, and directly fuel Everpures global expansion. What You'll Do Optimize Global Liquidity & Capital: Mastermind regional cash optimization strategies and intercompany funding structures to maximize capital efficiency, execute short-term investments, and minimize idle liquidity across international entities. Lead Banking Relationships & Governance: Serve as the strategic operational lead for international financial institutions, managing account lifecycles, user access controls, and periodic KYC compliance to maintain robust financial governance. Build Predictive Cash Models & Trade Finance: Develop high-accuracy liquidity forecasts and deploy AI-assisted analytics to evaluate cash variance, while managing Letters of Credit (LCs) to ensure trade compliance and support business scale. Drive Cross-Functional Excellence & Compliance: Partner with Accounting, FP&A, and Tax to execute month-end close reconciliations, support financial audits, and continuously automate treasury processes for maximum organizational speed. What You Bring Treasury Expertise: 6+ years of progressive corporate treasury experience managing complex international cash operations, intercompany liquidity, and trade finance within a global enterprise environment. Systems & Automation Mastery: Technical proficiency in ERP platforms, Treasury Management Systems (TMS), and AI-driven automation tools to modernize workflows, reporting, and forecasting accuracy. Strategic Collaboration & Execution: Outstanding analytical and cross-functional leadership skills, with a track record of translating financial insights into actionable outcomes alongside Legal, Tax, and Accounting partners. Work Location: We are primarily an in-office environment and therefore, you will be expected to work from the Bangalore office in compliance with Everpure s policies, unless you are on PTO, or work travel, or other approved leave.

title: Manager, Finance Operations
description:
Essential Job Duties and Responsibilities: Description: Footer Overall Purpose of The Job The Manager, Finance Operations oversees the day-to-day financial transaction cycle of Aspire Lifestyles India u2014 booking settlements, vendor payables, receivables, refunds, agent commissions, payment gateway operations, and the associated reconciliations. The role owns the operational close for the transaction cycle, ensures alignment of financial operations with corporate goals, safeguards controls and compliance, and partners with Operations, Sales, Technology and the wider Finance team (Reporting, Tax, Treasury) to enable accurate, timely and well-controlled financial outcomes. The role leads a team of Reconciliation Specialists and is a key contributor to process automation and continuous improvement across the Finance Operations function. Key RESPONSIBILITIES Own the end-to-end booking-to-settlement cycle: airline Billing and Settlement Plan reconciliations, GDS feeds, hotel and DMC payouts, aggregator settlements and traveller refunds. Oversee high-volume accounts payable and accounts receivable operations, ensuring accurate matching against booking inventories and supplier statements before release. Manage global agent commissions, incentive payouts and B2B ledger positions; ensure timely and accurate settlement in line with contractual terms. Oversee payment gateway operations, including reconciliation and monitoring of Pass-through and Merchant of Record transactions, chargebacks and gateway fees. Own the month-end and year-end close for the Finance Operations sub-ledgers (AP, AR, gateway, agent commissions), including accruals, provisions and reconciliations to the general ledger. Prepare and review unit-level and product-level profitability analyses for leadership; explain movements, margins and variances against plan. Deliver operational MIS, payment forecasts, aging analyses, settlement dashboards, gateway performance to the Head of Finance and business leadership. Coordinate closely with the Manager, Financial Reporting and the Tax function to ensure timely statutory reporting, tax compliance and consolidation inputs Design, operate and continuously improve internal controls over the transaction cycle (segregation of duties, approval matrices, exception reviews, reconciliation signoffs). Ensure compliance with Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS), company policies and Standard Operating Procedures across the operations team. Support GST, TDS and other statutory workings for AP/AR transactions in coordination with the Tax function; oversee resolution of GSTR-2B mismatches with vendors. Serve as the primary Finance Operations interface for internal, statutory and tax auditors; own timely closure of audit observations. Monitor and forecast cash outflows and inflows arising from the transaction cycle; partner with Treasury on funding requirements and FX exposures on cross-border settlements. Optimise working capital through disciplined payment runs, refund cycles, dispute resolution and receivables collection. Drive automation and simplification across the transaction cycle (invoice capture, reconciliation, workflow approvals, payment file generation, gateway reconciliation Standardise SOPs and drive measurable improvement in turnaround time, accuracy and control effectiveness Lead, develop and mentor a team of Reconciliation Specialists responsible for BSP, GDS, gateway, vendor and agent-commission reconciliations across the transaction cycle Key Metrics / Success Measures Timely and accurate operational close: sub-ledger close completed within 4-5 business days of month-end with zero material post-close adjustments. Payment discipline: on-time payment rate of [u2265 98%] and DPO within targeted range. BSP, gateway and agent-commission reconciliations completed monthly with all breaks investigated and cleared within the following month. Zero missed statutory due dates for AP/AR-related tax filings; clean statutory, internal and tax audits with no significant Finance Operations observations. Accurate and timely unit-level profitability reporting to leadership within agreed cadence. Job Profile Requirements 9 to 12 years of progressive experience in accounting and finance operations, including at least 3 years leading a team. Prior experience in the travel, hospitality or aviation sector strongly preferred, ideally with exposure to BSP settlements, GDS environments, DMC/aggregator payouts and payment gateway operations Strong working knowledge of SAP (FI/CO); comfort with finance systems integrations and reconciliation tools. Advanced MS Excel (pivot tables, XLOOKUP, SUMIFS, Power Query); familiarity with BI tools (Power BI / Tableau) an advantage. Sound knowledge of Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS) and Indian tax laws (GST, TDS, withholding on cross-border payments). Understanding of payment gateway mechanics, Pass-through vs Merchant of Record models, and card scheme / chargeback processes. Strong leadership presence with the ability to lead cross-functional and cross-regional teams. Excellent communication, interpersonal and presentation skills; able to engage confidently with leadership and external partners. Analytical and problem-solving mindset with strong attention to detail. Sound judgment in applying policy and controls while resolving exceptions pragmatically. High standards of confidentiality, integrity and ethics. Effective under time pressure and shifting priorities; comfortable managing multiple deadlines across close, audit and business cycles. Qualifications Bachelors degree in accounting/finance or equivalent experience. Chartered Accountant (Mandatory). Required Languages: Good spoken and written English language skills Travel Requirements: Not applicable / minimal.

Analyze data and find solutions. Create robust measurements and prediction models to create early warning systems. title: Manager Workforce Management - Dialer
description:
Position Summary The Operations Dialer Manager is responsible for the planning, execution, monitoring, and continuous optimization of outbound and inbound dialing strategies supporting first-party credit card collections. This role serves as a key liaison between Collections Operations, Workforce Management, Analytics/MIS, Compliance, Technology, clients, and third-party vendors, ensuring that account inventory, staffing, contact strategies, dialer capabilities, and business objectives are aligned to maximize collections performance while maintaining operational and regulatory compliance. The Operations Dialer Manager is expected to act as a subject matter expert in dialer strategy and collections operations, capable of representing the organization in discussions with clients, technology providers, telecommunications vendors, and internal stakeholders. The ideal candidate has strong experience in first-party credit card collections, understands delinquency-stage strategies and customer segmentation, and has hands-on knowledge of the LiveVox contact center and dialer platform. --- Key Responsibilities Dialer Strategy & Management Develop and execute daily, weekly, and monthly dialing strategies for first-party credit card collection portfolios. Configure and manage LiveVox campaigns, services, skill groups, dialing modes, account segmentation, and contact strategies. Determine appropriate dialing treatments based on delinquency stage, account risk, customer behavior, historical contactability, payment likelihood, and operational priorities. Optimize predictive, automated, manual, and agent-initiated dialing strategies based on portfolio requirements. Manage account penetration and attempt strategies to balance contact rates, collections performance, customer experience, and regulatory requirements. Evaluate campaign performance throughout the day and make real-time adjustments based on staffing, account inventory, penetration, contact rates, and collection results. Coordinate campaign reruns, prioritization strategies, and reassignment of account inventory when necessary. Identify opportunities to improve contact efficiency while reducing unnecessary or low-value dialing activity. --- Collections Operations Support collection strategies across various stages of delinquency, including early-stage, mid-stage, and late-stage credit card collections. Demonstrate working knowledge of key collections concepts, including: o Days Past Due and delinquency buckets o First Payment Default o Promise to Pay o Right Party Contact o Payment conversion o Account penetration o Customer contactability o Risk segmentation o Roll rates and forward flow Partner with Operations leadership to translate portfolio and client objectives into actionable dialer strategies. Identify opportunities to increase successful customer contacts and payment conversions without unnecessarily increasing dialing volume. Evaluate account inventory, staffing, agent utilization, and strategy performance to determine whether performance gaps are driven by manpower, account quality, contactability, dialer strategy, or operational execution. Provide recommendations to Operations leaders regarding staffing allocation, campaign priorities, account treatment, and contact strategy. --- Client, Vendor & Stakeholder Management Serve as a primary point of contact and dialer subject matter expert during discussions with clients, Operations leaders, technology teams, and third-party vendors. Participate in client meetings, business reviews, strategy sessions, and performance discussions related to collections and dialer performance. Present dialer performance, trends, strategy results, risks, and recommendations to internal and external stakeholders. Translate complex dialer and operational data into clear business insights appropriate for both technical and non-technical audiences. Work directly with clients to understand portfolio objectives, performance expectations, strategy requirements, and operational priorities. Partner with Operations stakeholders to ensure dialer strategies support frontline execution and overall collections objectives. Coordinate with vendors supporting: o Dialer and contact center technology o Telecommunications services o Branded Caller ID o Caller authentication o Phone intelligence and contactability o Data and analytics solutions Manage vendor-related issues, enhancement requests, testing, troubleshooting, and implementation activities. Evaluate proposed vendor solutions and new technologies based on operational value, cost, expected performance improvement, and implementation requirements. Coordinate testing and validation of new vendor features or dialer capabilities prior to production deployment. Escalate vendor performance, system, or service issues when necessary and track issues through resolution. Maintain productive relationships with clients and vendors while balancing operational requirements, technical limitations, compliance considerations, and business objectives. Support client inquiries and investigations involving dialer behavior, contact strategies, campaign configurations, or performance results. --- Performance Management & Analytics Monitor and analyze dialer and collections KPIs, including: o Attempts o Live Voice / Connect Rate o Right Party Contact Rate o RPC per Attempt o Promise to Pay Rate o Payment / Collection Rate o Contact-to-Payment Conversion o Accounts Worked o Penetration Rate o Average Handle Time o Talk Time o Wrap Time o Agent Occupancy o Idle / Ready Time o Abandonment Rate o Answering Machine Detection performance Perform trend, segmentation, and comparative analysis to identify opportunities for campaign optimization. Evaluate performance by delinquency segment, risk level, account population, time of day, agent group, site, and dialing strategy. Develop or support forecasting models for dialing volume, staffing requirements, contact rates, and expected collection outcomes. Conduct root-cause analysis when operational or client performance targets are missed. Develop clear recommendations and action plans based on analytical findings. Prepare performance summaries, dashboards, and executive-level presentations for internal leadership and clients. --- LiveVox Administration & Optimization Maintain strong working knowledge of LiveVox functionality, including: o Campaign and service configuration o Dialing strategies o Skill groups o Contact lists o Agent routing o Predictive dialing o Answering Machine Detection o Call disposition and result codes o Caller ID and branded calling solutions o Campaign pacing o Contact attempt controls o Reporting and Call Detail Records Troubleshoot campaign and dialing issues in coordination with Technology teams, LiveVox support, and other external vendors. Validate dialer configuration changes before implementation. Monitor system behavior to identify potential inefficiencies, routing issues, pacing concerns, or unusual contact patterns. Coordinate with LiveVox and other technology partners on platform enhancements, defects, upgrades, and new functionality. Support User Acceptance Testing and production validation for changes affecting dialer operations. --- Compliance & Risk Management Ensure dialing strategies comply with applicable company policies and regulatory requirements governing consumer communications and collections. Partner with Compliance, Legal, clients, and technology teams when implementing changes that may affect dialing frequency, calling windows, customer consent, contact treatment, or caller identification. Maintain appropriate controls around account attempts, contact frequency, time zones, phone number treatments, and calling hours. Monitor dialing activity for potential compliance risks and escalate concerns when necessary. Support audits and investigations involving dialer activity, customer contact attempts, and campaign configurations. Ensure changes requested by Operations, clients, or vendors are evaluated for potential compliance and customer-experience impact prior to implementation. --- Cross-Functional Leadership Serve as the primary dialer strategy partner for Operations leadership. Collaborate closely with: o Collections Operations o Client Leadership o Workforce Management o Business Analytics / MIS o Quality Assurance o Compliance o Information Technology o Telecommunications teams o LiveVox and other technology vendors Coordinate staffing and dialer capacity to ensure available agents are effectively utilized. Communicate strategy changes, campaign priorities, and performance expectations to Operations teams. Facilitate discussions between technical and operational stakeholders to ensure proposed solutions are practical and aligned with business objectives. Participate in performance reviews, client business reviews, strategy meetings, project discussions, and executive presentations. Influence stakeholders across multiple departments even when direct reporting relationships do not exist. --- Continuous Improvement Conduct controlled tests of new dialing strategies, account segmentation approaches, contact frequencies, campaign schedules, and dialing technologies. Measure pre- and post-implementation results to determine strategy effectiveness. Develop business cases for new dialer capabilities, vendor solutions, or process improvements. Identify opportunities for automation and improved reporting. Develop repeatable processes, dashboards, and decision frameworks for dialer management. Partner with clients and vendors to identify emerging opportunities to improve customer contactability and collection performance. Stay informed about emerging technologies affecting collections, including: o AI call screening o Branded Caller ID o Caller authentication o Predictive analytics o Customer contact optimization o Alternative communication channels o Phone intelligence and contactability solutions --- Required Qualifications Bachelor s degree in Business Administration, Finance, Operations Management, Analytics, or related field preferred. Minimum 3-5 years of experience in credit card collections, consumer finance, or contact center operations. Experience supporting or managing first-party credit card collections strongly preferred. Hands-on experience with LiveVox or a comparable predictive dialer/contact center platform. Experience interacting directly with clients, external vendors, and Operations stakeholders. Demonstrated ability to lead strategy and performance discussions with both internal and external business partners. Strong understanding of credit card delinquency and collections processes. Experience developing or managing outbound dialing strategies. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Excel. Experience interpreting large operational datasets and translating findings into actionable business recommendations. Strong verbal, written, and presentation skills. title: Senior Manager - Data & Analytics
description:
The Role We are looking for a hands-on leader to own the data, analytics, and AI portfolio end to end - and the team that builds it. You are the single point of accountability between business stakeholders and the analytics organization: gathering and pressure-testing requirements, turning ambiguous problems into a prioritized roadmap, and leading the developers, analysts, and data scientists who deliver scalable, trusted, widely adopted products. This is not a role that manages from a distance. You will be in the requirements sessions, the data model reviews, the SQL, the dashboard design critiques, and the model evaluations - and you will be measured on adoption and business outcomes, not backlog size or model sophistication. What You'll Do Team Leadership & Talent: Lead the team. Manage a talented team of senior and junior developers, analysts, and data scientists - setting direction on best practices, engineering standards, and alignment with team priorities. Develop people. Mentor team members, connecting their personal and professional goals to real career growth; set the standard for rigor and craft. Stakeholder Partnership & Requirements: Be the trusted partner. Serve as the primary interface to the different organizations and run structured discovery to elicit underlying needs, not feature requests. Write requirements that hold up. Translate business questions into testable specs: source systems, grain, metric definitions, SLAs, quality thresholds, and acceptance criteria. Drive a single source of truth for core metrics and arbitrate definitional conflicts. Simplify the complex. Navigate ambiguous, politically loaded problems and distill them into actionable messaging that aligns with business priorities and lands with executives. Prioritization. Roadmap & Datamart Strategy: Own the roadmap. Manage, prioritize, and align data, reporting, and analytics requirements with business needs, overseeing development and implementation. Make trade-offs explicit. Apply a consistent prioritization framework - value, reach, effort, risk, strategic fit - and communicate the rationale transparently, including to stakeholders you deprioritize. Shape strategy at the table. Play a key role in cross-functional committees defining data mart strategy, governance, and policy; invest ahead of demand in capabilities that make future requests cheaper to serve. Visualization & Experience Design: Design for the decision. Set the standard for how analytics is presented - choose the right visual for the question, build a clear hierarchy, and design every dashboard around the decision the user is trying to make rather than the data that happens to be available. Own the design system. Define and enforce visualization standards across the portfolio - chart conventions, color, typography, layout, naming, interaction patterns, and accessibility - so products look and behave consistently and stay maintainable as the team grows. Prototype, test, and prune. Wireframe and iterate with real users before building; validate with usage data and feedback, and retire dashboards that dont drive action. Technical Leadership: Warehouse, BI & Pipelines: Lead technically. Hands-on in advanced SQL on Snowflake, with the credibility to review the teams work rather than take it on faith. Design for scale. Oversee scalable pipelines and workflows that process large, diverse, unstructured datasets with high performance and reliability; automate cleaning, integration, and analysis in SQL and Python. Enable self-service. Champion governed datasets, semantic layers, and intuitive dashboards that let non-technical users answer their own questions - over one-off extracts and bespoke reports. Optimize what exists. Drive innovation in data architecture, dashboard performance, and cost efficiency; champion data quality and accuracy through lineage, testing, and clear ownership. Data Science, AI & Machine Learning: Set the AI agenda. Identify, size, and prioritize the use cases where ML and generative AI create real business value - and say no to the ones that dont. Deliver GenAI experiences. Build generative AI into the analytics stack - natural-language querying, conversational BI, automated insight generation, AI-assisted documentation and discovery. Adoption, Measurement & Communication: Measure what matters. Define success metrics for every product - adoption, time-to-insight, data freshness, decisions enabled, cost - and hold the team accountable to them. Drive adoption and clarity. Lead enablement through documentation, training, and change management; present insights, risks, and trade-offs to audiences from individual engineers to the executive staff. We are primarily an in-office environment and therefore, you will be expected to work from the Bengaluru office in compliance with Everpures policies, unless you are on PTO, or work travel, or other approved leave. What You Bring Experience & Leadership: 15+ years in analytics, business intelligence, data science, or data platform roles, including 4+ years directly managing teams. An advanced degree in statistics, data science, or computer science preferred. Demonstrated ownership of an enterprise data, BI, or analytics portfolio from requirements through production adoption, with evidence of business impact - plus a track record of solving complex problems and using data to influence senior stakeholders. Domain expertise in one or more of: finance, customer, or product. Experience with CRM and ERP datasets strongly preferred. Technical Depth: Advanced SQL - able to write, review, optimize, and debug complex analytical queries independently; deep experience with Snowflake or a comparable cloud data warehouse. Knowledge of Python, including package development and production-quality code standards. Hands-on with enterprise BI and semantic layer tools (Tableau, Power BI, Looker, ThoughtSpot) and what makes them perform at scale; working knowledge of governance, lineage, observability, and access control. Visualization & Design: Strong data visualization craft - fluent in chart selection, visual hierarchy, and the principles that separate a clear view from a cluttered one. Able to take a dense, ambiguous dataset and present it so an executive understands it in seconds. Genuine design sensibility: layout, whitespace, typography, purposeful color, and accessibility (including colorblind-safe palettes). A portfolio of dashboards or reports you designed is welcome. Experience establishing visualization standards or a design system across a BI portfolio, and comfort wireframing and iterating with users. Familiarity with UX principles and design tools such as Figma is a plus. Business & Communication Skill: Sophisticated stakeholder management: build consensus across functions, hold a position under pressure, and say no without damaging the relationship. Connect data and AI investments to business outcomes and articulate ROI in the language of the function being served. Excellent written and verbal communication - equally capable of a one-page decision memo and an executive presentation.

title: Regulatory Manager
description:
Role Summary Reporting to the Regional Regulatory Head, the Regulatory Manager, India & Middle East is responsible for defining and implementing regulatory strategies that enable compliant, timely and sustainable business growth across India and Middle East markets. The role serves as the primary regulatory business partner and regulatory voice for the IME organization. It influences portfolio, innovation, market-entry, product-classification and launch decisions by translating complex regulatory requirements into clear business options, risk assessments and actionable recommendations. The Regulatory Manager oversees a large and diverse product portfolio, balancing the operational demands of high-volume categories, particularly cosmetics, with the technical complexity and higher regulatory risk associated with OTC products, medical devices, dietary supplements, household products and electrical products. This position works closely with Commercial, Marketing, R&D, Quality, Legal, Supply Chain, Product Development and Global Regulatory Affairs to establish priorities, resolve regulatory barriers and balance compliance, business value, resource requirements and speed to market. It also leads interactions with distributors, consultants, agencies and, where appropriate, regulatory authorities. Success in this role requires a combination of regulatory leadership, sound technical judgment, portfolio management, execution discipline, cultural awareness and the ability to influence senior stakeholders without relying on direct authority. Strategy and Functional Expertise Develops and implements regulatory strategies that support compliant and sustainable business growth across India and the Middle East. Provides regulatory feasibility assessments for new products, market expansion, product classifications, claims and portfolio changes. Balances regulatory compliance, business risk and speed to market, particularly across cosmetics, OTC products, medical devices, dietary supplements, household products and electrical products. Translates complex regulatory requirements into clear business options and actionable recommendations. Applies sound regulatory judgment in ambiguous situations and identifies when technical or senior-level escalation is required. Monitors regulatory developments and assesses their potential impact on products, launches and business continuity. Maintains accurate regulatory documentation, performance metrics and management reporting. Promotes standardized, risk-based and efficient regulatory processes for a high-volume, multicategory portfolio. Leadership and Influence Acts as the regulatory voice and trusted business partner for India and Middle East leadership. Influences senior stakeholders and cross-functional teams without relying on direct authority. Leads discussions involving regulatory risk, portfolio priorities, market entry, product classification and speed-to-market decisions. Provides clear direction, removes obstacles and holds the regulatory team and stakeholders accountable for agreed deliverables. Develops team capability through coaching, feedback, knowledge sharing and stretch assignments. Builds effective relationships across Commercial, Marketing, R&D, Quality, Legal, Supply Chain, Product Development and Global Regulatory Affairs. Communicates complex issues clearly and persuasively, adapting the message to technical and nontechnical audiences. Demonstrates openness, curiosity and a willingness to listen to different perspectives, challenge assumptions and learn from local-market expertise. Promotes collaboration, inclusion and trust across organizational, geographic and cultural boundaries. Program Development / Project Management Leads regulatory programs and projects from strategy through implementation, ensuring clear scope, priorities, ownership and timelines. Manages multiple registrations, renewals, amendments, launches and regulatory-change initiatives simultaneously. Prioritizes projects according to regulatory risk, business impact, urgency and resource requirements. Monitors project progress, performance, deadlines, dependencies and spending. Anticipates regulatory barriers and coordinates timely actions to resolve issues. Works cross-functionally to identify market and distributor requirements and convert them into executable plans. Establishes practical governance, metrics and reporting to support timely decisions and stakeholder visibility. Manages consultants, agencies and other external partners, ensuring quality, confidentiality, accountability and effective use of resources. Identifies opportunities to simplify processes, reduce rework and improve regulatory productivity. Impact / Reach Supports a diverse, high-volume portfolio across India and multiple Middle East markets. Influences strategic and operational decisions involving regulated products, market access, launches and business continuity. Operates across country, regional and global teams, connecting local regulatory requirements with broader business priorities. Builds strong internal and external partnerships with business leaders, distributors, consultants, agencies and regulatory authorities. Demonstrates agility and cultural awareness when working across different markets, regulatory systems and business practices. Works openly and effectively in multicultural environments, respecting local perspectives while maintaining global standards. Creates clarity and alignment in complex situations where regulatory, commercial, technical and supply considerations may compete. Adjusts communication style, content and approach to meet the needs of different cultures, functions and levels of seniority. Education and Experience University degree from an accredited institution in pharmacy, chemistry, life sciences, engineering, regulatory affairs or another relevant technical field. Significant progressive experience in Regulatory Affairs within consumer health, consumer products or another multicategory regulated environment. Demonstrated experience supporting India, Middle East, GCC markets or similarly complex and diverse regulatory environments. Broad regulatory knowledge across at least two relevant categories, such as cosmetics, OTC medicines, medical devices, dietary supplements, household products, consumer products or electrical products. Experience managing high-volume portfolios and technically complex or ambiguous regulatory matters. Previous supervisory, people-management or team-lead experience. Experience working with distributors, consultants, agencies and regulatory authorities. Professional proficiency in written and spoken English; additional languages relevant to India and Middle East are advantageous. Experience working successfully with geographically dispersed and multicultural teams. Skills and Competencies Strong strategic thinking, regulatory judgment and business acumen. Results-oriented, action-oriented and accountable for delivery. Ability to make timely, high-quality decisions with incomplete or changing information. Excellent prioritization and portfolio-management capabilities. Strong project and program-management skills. Excellent verbal, written, presentation and negotiation skills. Ability to explain complex regulatory matters clearly, concisely and persuasively. Strong influencing and stakeholder-management capabilities. Demonstrated ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines simultaneously. Open-minded, curious and willing to explore alternative regulatory pathways and solutions. Comfortable asking questions, seeking different perspectives and constructively challenging established approaches. Culturally aware, adaptable and genuinely open to working with diverse teams, markets and ways of doing business. Strong collaboration, relationship-building and conflict-resolution skills. High attention to detail, organization, accuracy and confidentiality. Resilient and effective in complex, ambiguous and rapidly changing environments. Committed to continuous learning, process improvement and practical innovation.

title: Delivery Manager
description:
Anchanto | Job Description PBU Delivery & Agile Operations Manager - OMS Location: Pune, India | Reports to: Product Business Unit Head | Experience: 6+ Years | Type: Full time, Work from Office About the Role Anchanto is a global enterprise-grade B2B SaaS company. We provide cloud software for brands, retailers, and logistics providers to manage orders, inventory, marketplaces, fulfilment, parcel tracking, and omnichannel commerce. As Anchanto evolves toward integrated Product Business Units (PBUs), we need a leader who can run the delivery operating system of a business unit. This role combines multi-pod Scrum leadership, program delivery, resource and capacity planning, financial visibility, operational governance, and PBU administration. This is not a ceremony-only Scrum Master role. The person is expected to independently create structure, maintain a single view of all commitments, challenge unrealistic plans, hold senior stakeholders accountable, and ensure work gets delivered with speed, predictability, and quality. The role requires a strong presence with Product, Engineering, QA, DevOps, Customer Delivery, Support, and the PBU Head. Why This Role Exists The PBU model brings Product, Engineering, QA, Architecture, DevOps, Implementation, and Support closer together around a single product outcome. To make this model work, the PBU needs one owner for delivery rhythm, portfolio visibility, resource loading, risk management, operational discipline, and leadership reporting. This role exists to ensure that the PBU does not depend on fragmented trackers, informal follow-ups, or late escalations. What You Will Own The role owns nine areas. The expectation across all of them is the same: strong ownership, data over opinion, early visibility of risk, clear accountability, and reliable execution. Multi-pod Scrum and Agile delivery management Manage approximately 6 to 10 active Scrum teams or delivery pods in parallel, with the ability to scale the operating cadence as the PBU grows. Ensure effective sprint planning, backlog refinement, daily Scrum, reviews, retrospectives, and Scrum of Scrums without creating unnecessary ceremony. Ensure every pod has a clear sprint goal, ready backlog, acceptance criteria, realistic capacity plan, visible dependencies, and agreed Definition of Ready and Definition of Done. Monitor and improve commitment reliability, cycle time, lead time, throughput, scope churn, spillover, defect leakage, escaped defects, and release predictability. Improve velocity and flow sustainably without compromising quality or using story points as an individual productivity measure. Coach teams toward self-organisation while holding teams and leaders accountable for agreed process and delivery standards. Identify recurring blockers, late requirements, delayed QA, weak Jira hygiene, and process failures, and drive root-cause corrective action. Integrated delivery and portfolio planning Maintain one consolidated delivery plan across product roadmap, customer projects and customisations, technical debt, innovation, compliance, production incidents, and L3 support. Translate PBU priorities into executable milestones, pod plans, owners, dependencies, and resource requirements. Maintain visibility of planned versus actual progress, delivery confidence, critical path, scope changes, customer commitments, and roadmap displacement. Ensure customer-specific work does not silently displace roadmap commitments without an explicit business decision. Classify work as reusable product capability, hybrid product/customer work, or customer-specific customisation to support the right product and commercial decision. Support quarterly planning, monthly operating reviews, and major reprioritisation decisions with clear options and impacts. Maintain decision logs for material scope, priority, resource, budget, and date changes. Resource loading and capacity management Maintain a current capacity and allocation view across Product, Engineering, QA, Architecture, DevOps, Design, Implementation, and Support. Identify overload, underutilisation, shared-resource conflicts, skill bottlenecks, and single points of failure before they affect delivery. Recommend pod composition based on work requirements, available skills, and delivery risk. Present practical trade-off options when capacity is insufficient, including scope reduction, phased delivery, resequencing, date revision, temporary reallocation, hiring, or contracting. Prevent teams from accepting commitments without validated scope, dependencies, and confirmed capacity. Track planned versus actual utilisation and explain material variance. Delivery accountability and stakeholder leadership Act as the operating owner for PBU delivery and ensure commitments are converted into clear plans, owners, dates, and closure. Hold Product Managers, Engineering Managers, QA Leads, Architects, and other stakeholders accountable for agreed actions and standards. Conduct difficult delivery conversations when scope, dates, quality, resource availability, or process discipline are at risk. Challenge unrealistic commitments, incomplete requirements, unsupported dates, and unapproved customer promises with facts and alternatives. Escalate unresolved issues to Engineering Heads, the PBU Head, or leadership with impact, options, recommendation, and decision required. Maintain a visible and credible presence across the PBU; this role must not operate as a passive coordinator or status chaser. Financial and commercial governance Work with Finance and PBU leadership to track planned versus actual effort, budget consumption, forecast to complete, vendor or contractor cost, rework, and support cost. Maintain operational cost visibility for major roadmap initiatives and customer projects. Support customer-project margin and cost-to-value discussions by providing reliable delivery, effort, and forecast data. Identify material variance early and recommend corrective action. Ensure scope changes are reflected in effort, schedule, resource, and commercial discussions. Distinguish clearly between effort, cost, budget, billing, revenue, and margin. Formal accounting remains with Finance; this role owns the reliability of delivery inputs. Quality, release, and production governance Create and maintain PBU-level release-readiness criteria covering functional completion, regression, integration, security, performance, open defects, rollback, monitoring, and support readiness. Facilitate go/no-go discussions and provide a clear delivery recommendation based on risk and evidence. Track defect leakage, production incidents, rework, release failures, and recurring root causes. Ensure RCAs have clear owners, corrective actions, due dates, and verified closure. Include L3 support and production incidents in capacity plans so support demand is visible rather than treated as an unplanned interruption. Ensure delivery speed does not compromise quality, security, customer experience, or compliance. PBU administration and team operations Coordinate smooth onboarding for new PBU members, including access, tools, product orientation, process induction, stakeholder introductions, role clarity, and required training. Coordinate employee exits with HR, IT, Security, Finance, and functional managers, including access revocation, knowledge transfer, work reassignment, asset return, and documentation handover. Maintain the PBU roster, role map, allocation view, onboarding status, and critical knowledge coverage. Identify skill gaps and coordinate training, coaching, hiring, or external support. Ensure critical knowledge and delivery responsibility are not concentrated with one individual. Compliance and operational controls Track PBU obligations related to ISO, GDPR, information security, data retention, customer audits, internal controls, and market or regulatory requirements. Coordinate with Security, Legal, Compliance, Product, and Engineering owners to ensure actions and evidence are completed on time. Maintain compliance actions, evidence, owners, and due dates, and escalate overdue or high-risk items. Ensure compliance work is included in delivery plans and resource allocations rather than managed outside the operating plan. Support audit preparation and closure of observations for the PBU. Leadership reporting, systems, and continuous improvement Create a concise weekly PBU operating report covering delivery health, milestones, confidence, capacity, roadmap versus customer work, quality, production health, cost or effort variance, risks, recovery actions, and decisions required. Run weekly delivery reviews, cross-pod dependency reviews, release-readiness reviews, monthly leadership reviews, and quarterly planning retrospectives. Ensure Jira, Confluence, portfolio views, RAID logs, decision logs, and dashboards operate as trusted systems of record. Automate reporting, Jira hygiene, risk detection, meeting summaries, dependency tracking, and readiness checks wherever practical. Use AI and automation responsibly to improve delivery speed, data accuracy, and management visibility. Measure whether process changes improve predictability, quality, flow, and team effectiveness; remove governance that does not create value. Cross-Functional Operating Model Partner Primary partnership area PBU Head PBU priorities, investment choices, portfolio trade-offs, budget, and final escalation decisions Product Management Roadmap, problem definition, business value, requirements readiness, and product-versus-custom decisions Engineering Managers / Engineering Head Technical execution, engineering capacity, architecture, quality practices, skill development, and people leadership QA, DevOps, Security, and Architecture Release readiness, test coverage, environments, production health, security, compliance, and technical dependencies Customer Delivery, Sales, and Customer Success Customer commitments, implementation milestones, scope changes, commercial assumptions, and escalation Finance Budget, cost rates, forecast, project financials, margin visibility, and reconciliation HR, IT, and Administration Onboarding, exits, access, assets, employee operations, and workforce records What Good Looks Like After 12 to 18 Months The PBU has one trusted, current view of all roadmap, customer, technical, compliance, and support commitments. Six to ten parallel pods operate with predictable delivery rhythm, clear dependencies, and strong quality discipline. Leadership receives concise, decision-ready visibility rather than manual status collection. title: Fleet Manager
description:
Role & responsibilities 
 JOB DESCRIPTION FLEET MANAGER Company: Prashar Road Carriers Pvt. Ltd.
 Industry: Transportation and Logistics
 Department: Fleet Operations
 Reporting To: Head of Department / Director
 Location: Delhi NCR
 Employment Type: Full-Time About the Company Prashar Road Carriers Pvt. Ltd. is an established logistics company operating since 1993. The company provides Full Truck Load, Part Truck Load, local transportation, warehousing, air, rail and express cargo services across India. Job Summary The Fleet Manager will be responsible for the profitable, safe and efficient operation of the company’s owned commercial vehicles. The role includes vehicle planning, driver management, route monitoring, maintenance control, fuel management, documentation, trip profitability and daily reporting. The Fleet Manager will be personally accountable for ensuring maximum vehicle utilisation, minimum operating cost, timely deliveries and strict control over drivers, fuel, repairs, advances and vehicle documents. Key Responsibilities 1. Vehicle Planning and Utilisation Plan and deploy every vehicle to achieve maximum monthly running and revenue. Coordinate with the Traffic, Commercial, Marketing and Operations teams for availability of profitable loads. Minimise vehicle idle time, empty running and unnecessary detention. Arrange suitable return loads before or immediately after delivery. Ensure vehicles are not dispatched on commercially unviable trips without written approval. Maintain a daily availability and placement plan for all vehicles. Prioritise profitable movement on approved routes, including Delhi NCR, Gujarat, Vapi and Mumbai sectors. 2. Driver Management Recruit, verify and manage qualified heavy-commercial-vehicle drivers. Verify driving licence, Aadhaar, address, police verification, references and previous employment before deployment. Conduct daily communication with every driver regarding location, vehicle condition, delivery status and next movement. Ensure drivers follow assigned routes, scheduled halts and company instructions. Monitor driver attendance, conduct, driving discipline and performance. Prevent unauthorised vehicle use, route deviation, overloading and carrying of unauthorised goods or passengers. Enforce zero tolerance for alcohol, drugs, theft, misbehaviour and unsafe driving. Arrange replacement drivers promptly to avoid vehicle idling. Recommend driver incentives or disciplinary action based on measurable performance. 3. Trip and Route Monitoring Monitor every vehicle through GPS, SIM-based tracking, toll records and direct driver communication. Ensure a tracking link is generated and shared for every dispatched vehicle. Track loading, departure, transit, arrival, unloading and POD collection. Immediately escalate delays, breakdowns, accidents, route deviations or customer-related issues. Ensure drivers complete the required daily running while complying with road-safety and mandatory-rest requirements. Maintain accurate estimated and actual delivery timelines. Coordinate with customers, branches and unloading locations for timely vehicle release. 4. Fuel and Mileage Control Record fuel issued and purchased vehicle-wise and trip-wise. Monitor mileage against the prescribed vehicle benchmark. Cross-check fuel consumption with kilometres travelled, GPS records, load weight and route conditions. Prevent fuel theft, false bills, unauthorised refuelling and excess consumption. Investigate every case of mileage below the approved benchmark. Maintain fuel-card, cash-fuel and diesel-advance records. Submit a weekly vehicle-wise mileage and fuel-variance report. 5. Maintenance and Breakdown Management Maintain preventive-maintenance schedules for every vehicle. Ensure timely servicing, lubrication, tyre inspection, brake inspection and replacement of essential parts. Conduct or arrange pre-trip and post-trip vehicle inspections. Maintain vehicle-wise repair and maintenance history. Obtain estimates and approval before undertaking major repairs. Verify repair bills, replaced parts and workshop work before payment approval. Keep breakdown time and repair expenses under strict control. Maintain relationships with reliable workshops, mechanics, tyre vendors and roadside-assistance providers. Ensure spare tyres, tools, safety equipment and essential emergency items are available in every vehicle. 6. Tyre Management Maintain a tyre register containing tyre number, make, purchase date, fitting date, vehicle position and kilometres covered. Monitor tyre rotation, alignment, air pressure, retreading and replacement. Investigate premature tyre failure and driver negligence. Control tyre inventory and disposal of scrap tyres. Submit a monthly tyre-cost and tyre-performance report. 7. Documentation and Legal Compliance Ensure that the following documents remain valid and available:
 Registration Certificate Fitness Certificate National and state permits Insurance Pollution Under Control Certificate Road tax FASTag Driver’s licence E-way bill and consignment documents Any other statutory transport documents Maintain a document-expiry calendar and initiate renewals well in advance. Ensure compliance with applicable transport, road-safety and motor-vehicle regulations. Maintain records of challans, accidents, insurance claims and legal matters. Prevent dispatch of any vehicle or driver with expired or incomplete documents. 8. Trip Expenses and Advance Control Prepare and approve trip-expense estimates according to route, distance, tolls, fuel and applicable allowances. Record all advances issued to drivers. Ensure that every driver submits bills and settles the previous trip advance before receiving a new advance, except with written approval. Verify tolls, fuel bills, repair bills, loading/unloading expenses and other trip expenses. Prevent duplicate, inflated, unsupported or unauthorised claims. Submit completed trip sheets and supporting documents to Accounts within the prescribed timeline. 9. Delivery and POD Control Ensure safe and timely delivery of every consignment. Instruct drivers to obtain a properly signed and stamped Proof of Delivery. Ensure PODs are collected and submitted within 15 days of delivery or within the customer’s prescribed timeline. Maintain a daily pending-POD report. Coordinate with drivers, branches and customers to recover pending PODs. Immediately report shortages, damages, remarks, refusal of delivery or detention. Hand over PODs and trip documents to the ERP/Billing team against acknowledgement. 10. Accident and Emergency Management Respond immediately to accidents, breakdowns, theft, cargo damage and other emergencies. Arrange police intimation, photographs, survey, towing, repairs and alternate vehicles wherever required. Inform management, the customer, insurer and concerned authorities without delay. Protect the cargo and prevent further loss after an incident. Maintain complete accident and insurance-claim documentation. Conduct an internal review and recommend preventive measures after every major incident. 11. Cost and Profitability Control Prepare a vehicle-wise and trip-wise profitability statement. Monitor the following costs:
 Fuel Driver salary and allowance Toll and route expenses Repairs and maintenance Tyres Insurance and permits Detention and penalties EMI and depreciation, where applicable Empty-running cost Compare expected revenue with the complete trip cost before deployment. Identify loss-making vehicles, routes, customers and operating practices. Recommend measures to improve fleet profitability and asset utilisation. Work with the Commercial Manager to determine minimum viable freight for each route. Mandatory Daily Report The Fleet Manager must submit a written daily report every evening containing: Vehicle number Driver name and contact number LR/GR number Customer name Origin and destination Loading date Current vehicle location Current trip status Expected delivery date Actual delivery status POD status Advance paid Fuel purchased Kilometres travelled Mileage achieved Freight revenue Trip expenses Vehicle availability Breakdown or maintenance status Next-load planning Issues requiring management attention Failure to submit the daily report without valid authorisation may be treated as failure to perform assigned duties and may affect attendance and performance evaluation. Key Performance Indicators Performance will be evaluated on: Vehicle utilisation percentage Loaded kilometres versus empty kilometres Monthly revenue per vehicle Trip-wise and vehicle-wise profitability Fuel efficiency and mileage variance On-time pickup and delivery percentage Average vehicle idle time Return-load arrangement Maintenance cost per kilometre Number and duration of breakdowns Tyre life and tyre cost per kilometre Driver retention and discipline Accident and challan frequency Timely settlement of driver advances Percentage of PODs received within 15 days Accuracy and punctuality of daily reports Compliance with documentation and renewal deadlines Required Qualifications and Experience Graduate or diploma holder; transport or automobile qualification preferred. Minimum 5 years of relevant experience managing commercial trucks or heavy vehicles. Practical knowledge of 12-wheel, 14/15-wheel and multi-axle vehicles is preferred. Strong understanding of diesel consumption, mileage, tyres, repairs, permits, tolls and trip expenses. Experience managing drivers and resolving on-road operational issues. Knowledge of major transport routes, especially Delhi NCR, Gujarat and Maharashtra. Comfortable using GPS systems, WhatsApp, email, Excel and transport ERP software. Ability to prepare daily MIS and vehicle-wise profitability reports. Willingness to remain available for urgent fleet matters outside normal working hours. Essential Skills Strong leadership and driver-handling ability High level of honesty and accountability Commercial and cost-control mindset Knowledge of vehicle maintenance Route and load-planning ability Negotiation and vendor-management skills Crisis-management capability Accurate documentation and reporting Basic Excel and ERP proficiency Clear written and verbal communication Behavioural Expectations The Fleet Manager must: Protect company vehicles, cargo, money and reputation. Maintain complete transparency in fuel, repairs, advances and vendor dealings. Never accept commissions or personal benefits from workshops, fuel stations, drivers or vendors. Avoid providing false vehicle locations, fabricated reports or incorrect expense information. Immediately disclose accidents, cargo damage, theft, breakdowns and financial irregularities. Maintain confidentiality of company rates, customers and operational information. Follow management instructions and cooperate with all departments. title: Lead Engineer - Engineering Planner & Scheduler
description:
Job Description Summary The Lead Engineering Planner will be responsible for developing, integrating, and maintaining high-quality engineering project schedules across HDNU Gas Power Engineering. This role supports proposal, contract, and execution phases, ensuring schedule rigor, transparency, and alignment with business objectives. The position plays a key role in improving planning maturity, schedule quality, and delivery performance across projects and portfolios. Job Description Roles and Responsibilities Engineering & Project Scheduling Develop, release, and maintain complex, integrated engineering project schedules using Primavera P6, ensuring alignment with scope, execution strategy, and contractual requirements. Execute project schedules for assigned Gas Power Business scopes (including Gas Turbine/Generator/Steam Turbine/HRSG and Balance of Plant engineering), ensuring schedule integrity throughout the project lifecycle. Convert proposal and tender schedules into fully integrated contract schedules, adjusting activity logic, durations, and sequencing based on finalized engineering scope. Prepare and manage Tender Time Schedules (TTS), Overall Time Schedules (OTS), Master Time Schedules (MTS), System Time Schedules (STS), and portfolio-level schedules as required. Establish and maintain baseline schedules, manage revisions (Rebaseline), and control schedule changes through formal change logs. Proposal & Contract Support Partner with ITO and Proposal teams to define engineering support requirements, develop schedule assumptions, scope matrices, and delivery sequences. Participate in deviation and clarification meetings, supporting schedule alignment during proposal and contract finalization. Provide schedule inputs for contract negotiations and support preparation of contract documentation. Schedule Control & Performance Monitoring Monitor, update, and control project schedules based on engineering progress inputs (including PLM interfaces). Identify and analyze critical and near-critical paths, float consumption, and schedule risks; proactively recommend mitigation and recovery actions. Evaluate schedule impacts resulting from customer-requested scope changes and support Extension of Time (EOT) and as-impacted schedule analyses. Perform micro-planning for critical or delayed work packages and develop what-if scenarios to support recovery planning. Reporting, Analytics & Communication Prepare and release project dashboards, KPIs, progress reports, and management presentations for steering committees and senior leadership. Develop and maintain S-Curves, progress measurement systems (Earned value management), and forecast completion metrics for engineering scopes. Issue weekly look-ahead schedules, monthly progress reports, and on-time delivery (OTD) performance reports. Track and report engineering and customer deliverable milestones (LD). Clearly communicate schedule status, risks, and recovery plans to cross-functional stakeholders. Collaboration & Continuous Improvement Partner with senior engineering planners to define and continuously improve planning standards, templates, and data management practices. Collaborate across Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, Manufacturing, Finance, and external vendors to maintain schedule rigor and execution discipline. Capture lessons learned and planning best practices during project close-out to support continuous improvement across HDNU Gas Power Engineering. Required Qualifications Bachelor s degree in Mechanical or Electrical engineering. Experience in Engineering Planning, Project Planning, or Equipment Planning within complex industrial or EPC environments. Strong hands-on experience with Primavera P6 scheduling and reporting. Desired Characteristics Demonstrated leadership in planning, scheduling, and cross-functional coordination. Proven expertise in baseline management, float analysis, schedule optimization, and risk- based planning. Strong analytical skills with the ability to translate complex schedule data into actionable insights. Excellent written and verbal communication skills; confident presenting to senior leadership and customers. High energy, self-starter mindset with a consistent track record of delivery and execution excellence. Experience supporting proposal, contract, and execution phases in large-scale power or industrial projects. Demonstrated behaviors aligned with The Vernova Way. Additional Information Relocation Assistance Provided: No

The company operates four business units, known as Strategic Business Units - Honeywell Aerospace, Honeywell Building Technologies (HBT), Safety and Productivity Solutions (SPS), and Honeywell Performance Materials and Technologies. We are uniquely positioned to blend physical products with software to support connected systems that improve buildings, factories, utilities and aircraft and that enable a safer, more comfortable and more productive world. Our solutions enhance the quality of life of people around the globe and create new markets and even new industries.
